dominant_strengths: Confident serif headline against warm cream creates a calm, premium banking tone distinct from typical fintech blue
Product UI screenshot is dense yet legible, signaling craft and reinforcing the 'radically different' claim with evidence
Clear conversion hierarchy: headline, subcopy, email capture, then demo CTA flow naturally without visual clutter
dominant_weaknesses: Headline claims 'radically different' but the layout is a conventional centered hero—copy overpromises versus visual distinctiveness
Purple gradient fade behind the laptop feels generic and slightly muddy against the cream, weakening the otherwise refined palette
FDIC disclaimer overlay awkwardly bisects the product image, undermining craft and the perceived edge of the screenshot
fix_priorities: Reposition or restyle the FDIC disclosure so it doesn't crop the dashboard hero image
Introduce a more distinctive hero composition (asymmetry, typographic detail) to match the 'radical' verbal promise
Refine the purple backdrop with cleaner color stops or a textural element to elevate the reflective layer
rationale.norman_balance: Strong behavioral clarity and decent visceral warmth, but reflective payoff is undercut by a hero that doesn't live up to its own headline.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—it reads unmistakably as Mercury's premium-but-approachable fintech banking pitch with product proof and clear conversion path.
